entries.message: the attribute `{name}` was given {kind}. An attribute value is a string and nothing else.
entries.fix: If the element is meant to RECEIVE this value, bind a property instead — `{property}` — which is how a custom element takes anything that is not text. If it is meant to be read as text, convert it where you know what it means: `date.toISOString()`, `list.join(' ')`. A Date in particular serializes with the SERVER's timezone on one side and the browser's on the other, so it will not survive hydration.

entries.message: a child position was given `{value}`, which renders as the word "{value}" — the usual cause is `${cond && …}` with a false `cond`.
entries.fix: Write `${cond ? … : null}`, or `${(cond && …) || null}`; `null` and `undefined` are the values that render nothing. If you meant to display the boolean, say so with `${String(value)}` and this goes quiet.

entries.message: <{tag}> binds `.{name}`, which replaces the element's content, and also has content of its own — markup or a child binding, which the write would strand.
entries.fix: Bind one or the other: the property alone (`{alone}`), or the content alone.

entries.message: observes an attribute whose prop, `{prop}`, is one the platform's element already REFLECTS — this tag's accessor replaces it, so setting `el.{prop}` no longer does what the platform's does (it no longer writes the attribute).
entries.fix: Observe it only if the component owns that attribute; otherwise read it in the render with `host.getAttribute(…)`.

entries.message: shares the prop `{prop}`, whose default is a {type} — and the attribute arrives as a STRING, so the prop changes type the moment it appears.
entries.fix: Give the prop a string (or null) default, and convert in the render; or keep the attribute and the prop under different names.

entries.message: expected an array of attribute names and received {received}.
entries.fix: List them: `attributes: ['label', 'data-count']` — each arrives as a prop (`label`, `dataCount`).

entries.message: an `adoptedCallback` costs every element of this tag its creation (measured +7.4% on create10k), and it is installed.
entries.fix: Keep it only if moving elements between documents needs it.

entries.message: `{name}` is core's own on a define-made class, so this one is never installed (in any build).
entries.fix: Put connect-time work in the setup; for work on removal, a `disconnectedCallback` in methods runs as the teardown hook.

entries.message: is not a function, so it is installed as a plain value shared by every instance — and a getter ran ONCE, here.
entries.fix: Methods are functions; a value that changes per element is a prop (`props: { name: default }`).

entries.message: never fires: the class observes no attributes, and it is installed anyway.
entries.fix: Declare them: `define({ tag, attributes: ['label'] }, …)` — each then arrives as a prop.

entries.message: `{name}` is also a method, and the prop wins (it is installed after the methods), in every build.
entries.fix: Give the method or the prop another name.

entries.message: this default is an object that cannot be copied per element (a Set, a Map, a class instance), so EVERY element of the tag shares this one — a change through one shows in all.
entries.fix: Declare it `null` and create it in the setup (`props: { selected: null }`, then `host.selected = new Set()`), or pass it in; arrays and plain objects are copied per element.

entries.message: expected an object of names and their defaults and received {received}, so no prop is declared.
entries.fix: Name each prop with its default: `props: { heading: '', items: [] }`.

entries.message: is skipped, in every build: written onto the class prototype it would replace a prototype instead of adding a {kind}.
entries.fix: Rename the key. An own `__proto__` comes from `JSON.parse` or `Object.defineProperty`, never from an object literal.

entries.message: the second argument is the SETUP, a function, and received {received}.
entries.fix: Pass the setup after the tag or the options: `define('x-card', (host) => () => html`…`)`.

entries.message: replaces the platform's `{name}` for every user of these elements — scripts, libraries and the browser's own callers — and it is installed.
entries.fix: Give it a name of its own, unless replacing the platform member is the point.

entries.message: expected a custom element name — a string with a hyphen, not at the start — and received {received}.
entries.fix: Name it the way the platform requires: `define('x-card', setup)` or `define({ tag: 'x-card' }, setup)`.

entries.message: is already defined by another copy or version of {pkg}, so the first is kept.
entries.fix: Align the versions, or import {pkg}/{entry} and define it under your own tag.

entries.message: @{name} is not an event <{tag}> fires — did you mean @{best}? (In JSX, on{name} compiles to @{name}.)
entries.fix: A custom event by this name is fine, and this is said only in development.

entries.message: is shaped like a template but was not made by html`` — rendered as text.
entries.fix: A template from data (JSON, or html([markup])) is never markup; for trusted markup, bind it: <div .innerHTML=${markup}>.

entries.message: received a bound property `.{key}` (or `!{key}`), but its class declares `{key}` as a getter with no setter — the value cannot be delivered and the binding is ignored.
entries.fix: Add a setter, or stop binding it.

entries.message: binds the `{name}` attribute, which runs its value as code — refused.
entries.fix: Bind a function as an event instead: {event}.

entries.message: a 'template' or 'element' module (namespaces, elements, slots) was wired after the renderer had already built templates — those never ask it, and keep rendering without it.
entries.fix: Wire it beside the renderer, before the first render.

entries.message: an attribute name cannot be an expression — `{written}` is read by the parser before any value exists.
entries.fix: A name known only at runtime is a spread: `${spread({ [`{written}`]: {given} })}` (from @verajs/renderer/spread).

entries.message: @{name} was given a {type}, which cannot listen — the event will do nothing.
entries.fix: Pass a function, or an object with a handleEvent method. A missing handler is `undefined` or `false`, both of which are fine; this is neither.

entries.message: binds `{written}`, which would replace the element's own prototype and destroy it — no property write does this, and no use of it is legitimate.
entries.fix: The binding is ignored.

entries.message: `{name}` was given a javascript: URL — refused, and the attribute removed.
entries.fix: A bound URL is data, and data must never become code.

entries.message: `{name}` controls only ONE selection here, and a selection the user adds is kept — it is not controlled.
entries.fix: Bind `?selected=${…}` on each <option> to control every selection.

entries.message: its setup returned {kind}, not a render function, so it rendered once and will never update.
entries.fix: Return a render function — `return () => html`…`;` — the setup runs once, the render on every change.

entries.message: binds the `srcdoc` attribute, which renders its value as an HTML document — refused.
entries.fix: If the markup is trusted and sanitized, bind the property: `{property}`.

entries.message: style expects a STRING, not an object.
entries.fix: Build the string: {example}.

entries.message: expected a template literal and received {received}.
entries.fix: It is a tagged template — write {tag}`{example}`, not {tag}('{example}').

entries.message: <{tag}> is already defined; the platform refuses a second definition of a tag and throws next.
entries.fix: Define each tag once, at module level. A live swap of a component while developing needs the development swap module, wired before the first define.

entries.message: an expression in tag position (`<${…}>`) cannot be a tag name — a tag name must be a tag value.
entries.fix: Use `tag`h1`` from @verajs/renderer/tag, with that entry's `html`.

entries.message: a template inside a text-only element (`<style>`, a JSON `<script>`, `<title>`, `<textarea>`, or never-shown content: `<noscript>`, `<iframe>`) is never shown as markup — its content is text.
entries.fix: Render a string there; a list of strings is joined.

entries.message: an object holding a real template literal's `strings` but no `_$litType$` — a wrapper only `@verajs/core`'s `hold` or `tag` builds — is no template here: it renders as the text any object renders as, `[object Object]`.
entries.fix: Render the `html` result itself; `@verajs/core` renders such a wrapper as its template.

entries.message: a template cannot end inside a tag — the parser drops an unfinished tag.
entries.fix: Close the tag inside the template.

entries.message: `{key}` is not an option, so it was ignored.
entries.fix: The options are {list}.

entries.message: the value bound to `{name}` was replaced while the element upgraded. A class field is the usual cause: at ES2022 `{name}?: …` emits `{name};`, which runs during upgrade and overwrites whatever was set beforehand.
entries.fix: Write it `declare {name}?: …` instead. A component that calls init() adopts bound properties automatically and never sees this; this element did not. Ignore this if the component replaced the value on purpose.

entries.message: <{tag}> is a void element — it has no end tag and takes no children, so {fate}; refused.
entries.fix: Move the children out, or use an element that takes content.

entries.message: <{tag}> was built as {built} and placed inside <{host}>, where it will not render.
entries.fix: {advice}
